hero.title: Cook. Plate. Sprinkle. Eat.
hero.subtitle: A Thrakian family recipe of toasted sesame, sea salt, red pepper, cumin and thyme — finished by hand in small batches in Florida.

category.title: Not a cooking spice. A finishing ritual.
category.description: Most spice blends are designed to cook with heat. Tuz Biber is made to meet the plate after the flame, adding color, salt, and savor where flavor can shine.
bullets: Cook first, then finish with the final note.
Adds texture and a savory snap without overpowering the dish.
Built for eggs, burrata, grilled vegetables, meats, and warm bread.

founderStory.title: From Keşan to Florida, a family table in every jar.
body: The story begins in Keşan, in the Thracian region where food is guided by memory, season and generosity.
Chef İnan Doğru carried that family table to Florida and began blending small batches inspired by his home kitchen and the rhythm of the coast.
founderStory.quote: A good finish should feel like a last welcome at the table.

cultural.title: Rooted in the Turkish table. Unmistakably modern.

faq.title: Questions people ask before the first jar.

items.question: Is this meant to be cooked in the pan?
items.answer: No. Tuz Biber is intended as a finishing seasoning, added after the food is cooked and plated.

items.question: Why are there only five ingredients?
items.answer: So the flavor reads cleanly and intentionally — warm, savory, textural, and never crowded.

items.question: Can I use it on eggs and bread?
items.answer: Yes. It works especially well with eggs, burrata, vegetables, grilled meats and warm olive oil bread.

items.question: When will the next release happen?
items.answer: We release in small batches. Joining the list is the best way to hear about the next run before it sells out.

storyPage.title: A family finishing ritual from Thrace to Florida.
storyPage.intro: Born from a table that never rushed the final seasoning.
body: In Keşan, the final sprinkle was always a moment of care — never an afterthought.
Chef İnan Doğru brought that lesson to Florida and refined it into a modern small-batch blend for generous plates and memorable hospitality.

ingredientPage.title: We keep the list short and the finish honest.
ingredientPage.intro: Five ingredients, all tuned to create warmth, texture and clean salinity.
body: Toasted sesame brings comfort and crunch.
Sea salt sharpens the flavor while cumin and thyme deepen the aroma.
Red pepper adds heat and color without dominating the bowl or the plate.

howToUsePage.title: Before heat, after care.
howToUsePage.intro: The dish should be cooked, plated, and then finished with a final, deliberate sprinkle.
body: Use it over warm eggs, grilled vegetables, roasted potatoes, burrata, meats and buttery bread.
Think of it as a finishing layer: not a seasoning to hide behind, but a flourish that completes the plate.
